Weather

Usually a crosswind You ride SSE; early-September wind here runs from the WSW at 6.5 mph, and holds that direction 90% of the time. Mean of 2015–2024 September, 9:00–17:00, at the day’s midpoint. What to expect, not a forecast.

The day at a glance

The Pajaro Valley behind Watsonville is one of the largest strawberry and cane-berry districts in the country; the low ground either side of the road is berries under plastic for much of the year. Nearer the coast it turns to artichokes and brussels sprouts, and at Moss Landing the route passes Elkhorn Slough, a tidal estuary and one of the better bird sites on this coast.

Worth looking up for

  • Flat coastal day along Monterey Bay, the gentlest climbing of the trip at 1,640 ft.
  • Moss Landing sits right on the route at roughly halfway — a good lunch stop.

What to watch for

  • Nothing steeper than 3.5% anywhere on the route — the least climbing of the whole trip at 1,640 ft.

Stops along the way

Mapped in OpenStreetMap and carried in the GPX as waypoints, so they show on a head unit too. Distances are miles from the start. Tap a name for Google Maps, or the arrow for Apple Maps. Not verified on the ground — opening hours and whether a tap actually runs are anyone’s guess. A star marks a stop somebody picked by hand and vouched for, rather than one the OpenStreetMap query happened to return. Everything else here is within a quarter mile of the line; the few that are further say how far.
